query: For AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additively manufactured miniature components, what single intervention could overcome the residual thermal stresses, degraded mechanical properties, and processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes? Formulate one hypothesis that specifies the intervention and mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions, states the applicable processing window, geometry, and test conditions, identifies supporting prior evidence, and describes a falsification experiment.

generation.material_initial_state: Homogeneous gas-atomized AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder, sieved to 10–60 μm, dispersed in an acrylate-based photocurable resin to form a slurry and DLP-printed into layered green bodies.
generation.intervention: The DLP-printed green bodies were debound under either oxygen-rich ambient air or an oxygen-deficient environment maintained by continuous mechanical-pump evacuation, then solid-state sintered at 800, 1000, 1050, or 1100 °C for 24 h. Debinding included 1 h holds at 300 and 450 °C followed by heating to 500 °C.
generation.conditions: Specimens were printed with a 405 nm source at 19.57 mW/cm², 100 s exposure, 70 μm layers, and 20 layers, then ultrasonically cleaned in ethanol. Atmosphere-dependent debinding and subsequent furnace sintering were compared over 800–1100 °C; a 600 °C sample disintegrated and was excluded from the main sintering analysis.
generation.structural_mediator: Increasing Mo produced Mo-induced FCC lattice distortion and increasing amounts of a hard, Mo-rich tetragonal σ phase, while Ag, Ni/MoS2, and Cr2O3 remained distributed mainly along matrix-powder boundaries. During sliding, Ni/MoS2-Ag-rich lubricating films operated at low-to-medium temperature, whereas oxide/molybdate tribofilms formed at high temperature; Mo1 developed a particularly continuous, dense glaze at 800 °C containing NiO and Ag2MoO4, Ag2Mo4O13, and Ag2Mo2O7.
generation.mechanism: Dissolved Mo impedes dislocation motion through solid-solution strengthening, and the hard σ phase suppresses plastic deformation and scratching through second-phase strengthening. At lower temperatures, layered MoS2 supplies a low-shear film and soft Ag reduces adhesion, although thermal softening and rough wear tracks at 200–400 °C hinder formation of a continuous lubricant layer. At 600–800 °C, oxidation and tribochemical reactions generate layered silver molybdates and other oxides; compaction of these products into a glaze separates the matrix from the counterface and reduces interfacial shear and material removal.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to oxygen-rich debinding, oxygen-deficient debinding is reported to produce earlier densification and comparable maximum compressive strength at a 50 °C lower sintering temperature, while reducing debinding-induced surface cracking.
generation.baseline: DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi specimens debound in oxygen-rich ambient air and sintered for 24 h; these required 1100 °C for full consolidation and approximately 5.1 MPa compressive strength.
generation.boundary: The result applies to the studied DLP-printed AlCrFeNiSi powder/resin system and the specified debinding schedule, atmospheres, and 24 h sintering treatments. Below about 1000 °C elemental diffusion remained limited, while at 1100 °C oxygen-deficient samples developed stripe-like precipitates attributed to localized softening or melting of fine particles without oxide protection.

falsification_experiment.design: SEM of top, side, and polished cross-sectional surfaces was used to assess cracks, porosity, particle interfaces, layered morphology, and consolidation; EDS mapping quantified carbon, oxygen, aluminum, nickel, and interfacial redistribution; compression testing with an MTS universal testing machine measured strength versus atmosphere and sintering temperature.
measurements: SEM of top, side, and polished cross-sectional surfaces was used to assess cracks, porosity, particle interfaces, layered morphology, and consolidation; EDS mapping quantified carbon, oxygen, aluminum, nickel, and interfacial redistribution; compression testing with an MTS universal testing machine measured strength versus atmosphere and sintering temperature.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the predicted outcome is not observed relative to the baseline, the hypothesis is rejected.
